messages:
Nina (support): Heads up — sales needs a temporary allowlist for a partner demo tomorrow, ~2k reqs over 45m. Can we do a safe fast-path?
Alex (eng): What's the exact scope? per-key or org-wide?
Nina (support): Per-key for the demo API key. Customer is PII-free, just generates text. Tony says needs it by 9am PT.
Tony (sales): yep, very time-sensitive. demo slot booked. Need the ability to hit higher qps for 30-60m.
Sam (product): I want to avoid ad-hoc manual exceptions that bypass audit. Can we formalize as "ephemeral leases" in the console with required approver + ticket link?
Maria (security): Strong +1. Requirements: (1) TTL on the allowlist entry, (2) mandatory approver from support or security, (3) immutable audit record stored in event log, (4) deny-list fallback if abuse detected.
Alex (eng): Proposed flow: support opens a ticket in Zendesk with customer and reason, then run admin action: `rbac allowlist create --key <key> --ttl 60m --reason "demo-<ticket>" --approver @nina`
Alex (eng): The backend will emit an event: `allowlist.grant` with metadata (actor, ticket, expires_at). We already have hooks in the audit stream so that should be straightforward.
approvals-bot: Approval required: Nina (support) must approve the allowlist grant for key abc123.
Nina (support): Approved via ticket #2451. Adding approval comment.
approvals-bot: Grant recorded. audit_id=evt_20260318_001. Expires in 60m.
Jen (sre): Can we add automatic throttling rule if aggregate qps > X? i.e. still protect shared infra. Otherwise a single demo could spike GPU usage.
Alex (eng): Yep — implement soft cap for ephemeral leases: rate limit = min(configured_burst_limit, 5x baseline_per_key) and global circuit-breaker if infra exceeds 80% utilization; circuit trips and all ephemeral leases go into read-only mode.
Maria (security): Also log outgoing payload size and destination IPs for the lease window (retention 90d). We need evidence if we later detect abuse.
Sam (product): UX note: in console, show a badge on the API key with lease state and a link to the ticket + expiration timestamp. Make it easy to revoke.
Tony (sales): Will that be fast enough for demos? We need a self-serve button for support to pre-approve scheduled demos (timebox window).
Alex (eng): We can add a "request scheduled lease" form that creates a draft and triggers an approval workflow. Implement as a short-term feature patch this sprint.
Jen (sre): Telemetry: tag all requests with `ephemeral_lease_id` so we can chart cost and latency per-lease in Console. Also add alert if per-lease error rate > 5% for 5m.
Maria (security): Final checklist before we ship this: audit logs hooked to SIEM, TTL enforced server-side, immutable approver chain, and a rollback playbook.
Sam (product): I'll draft the console copy and the support runbook. Nina, can you confirm support training?
Nina (support): Yep, will run a 15m training tomorrow at 8:15am PT and paste the runbook into #help.
Alex (eng): I'll put together the minimal CLI/web endpoints and a DB migration to store lease metadata. PR later today.
approvals-bot: Note: Any manual allowlist modifications require two approvers if duration > 4h.
Tony (sales): Thanks team — appreciate the fast turnaround.
Jen (sre): Quick follow-up: add a metric that counts ephemeral leases per-org so we can detect heavy reliance and maybe suggest Dedicated plans.
Sam (product): Good idea — include a quota warning in Console when ephemeral-lease-hours for an org > 10h/week.
Nina (support): Ticket #2451 updated: lease issued for demo key abc123, expires 60m after activation.
Alex (eng): Closing loop: I'll attach the PR/endpoint URL here once merged.
Sam (product): Thanks everyone.
